# Phasors to Time

For any phase $x\in{a,b,c}$,  
$$
\boxed{v_x(t)=\sqrt{2}\Re\big\{V_xe^{j\omega t}\big\} =\sqrt{2}|V_x|\cos\big(\omega t+\angle V_x\big).}
$$

# Using the seq→abc map

$$
\begin{bmatrix}V_a\\V_b\\V_c\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1 & a^2 & a\\ 1 & a & a^2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}V_0\\V_1\\V_2\end{bmatrix},\quad a=e^{j\frac{2pi}{3}}=e^{j120^\circ}
$$

and setting $V_0=0$, you get the per-phase time signals as the sum of a positive-sequence contribution and a negative-sequence contribution:

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_a(t)
&= \sqrt{2}\Re\big\{(V_1+V_2)e^{j\omega t}\big\}
&= \sqrt{2}\big[|V_1|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_1) +|V_2|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_2)\big]\\[4pt]
v_b(t)
&= \sqrt{2}\Re\big\{(a^2V_1+aV_2)e^{j\omega t}\big\}\ 
&= \sqrt{2}\big[|V_1|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_1+240^\circ) +|V_2|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_2+120^\circ)\big]\\[4pt]
v_c(t)
&= \sqrt{2}\Re\big\{(aV_1+a^2V_2)e^{j\omega t}\big\}\ 
&= \sqrt{2}\big[|V_1|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_1+120^\circ) +|V_2|\cos(\omega t+\angle V_2+240^\circ)\big]
\end{aligned}
$$

# Specialize to the "photon" choice

$$
V_1 = r e^{+j\phi},V_2=r e^{-j\phi}
$$  

Plugging
$$
|V_1|=|V_2|=r,\quad\angle V_1=+\phi,\quad\angle V_2=-\phi
$$

$$ 
\boxed{ \begin{aligned}
v_a(t) &= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi)+\cos(\omega t-\phi)\big] = 2\sqrt{2}r\cos\phi\cos\omega t,\\[6pt]
v_b(t)
&= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi+240^\circ)+\cos(\omega t-\phi+120^\circ)\big]\
&= 2\sqrt{2}r\cos(\phi+60^\circ)\cos(\omega t+\pi),\\[6pt]
v_c(t)
&= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi+120^\circ)+\cos(\omega t-\phi+240^\circ)\big]\ &= 2\sqrt{2}r\cos(\phi-60^\circ)\cos(\omega t+\pi).
\end{aligned}}
$$

Notes

- Used $\cos A + \cos B = 2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}$.
    
- You can also write $\cos(\omega t+\pi) = -\cos\omega t$. So $v_b, v_c$ are $\pi$ out of phase with $v_a$, with amplitudes set by $\cos(\phi\pm 60^\circ)$. This is the "split-phase" feel.
    

# What if you **flip the sign of $V_1$**?

A sign flip is $V_1\mapsto -V_1$, i.e. add $180^\circ$ to $V_1$'s phase. In time-domain formulas above, just shift the $V_1$ terms by $\pi$:

$$ \begin{aligned}
v_a'(t) &= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi+\pi)+\cos(\omega t-\phi)\big]\\
&= \sqrt{2}r\big[-\cos(\omega t+\phi)+\cos(\omega t-\phi)\big]\\
&= 2\sqrt{2}r\sin\phi\sin\omega t,\\[6pt]
v_b'(t) &= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi+240^\circ+\pi)+\cos(\omega t-\phi+120^\circ)\big]\\
&= 2\sqrt{2}r\sin(\phi+60^\circ)\sin(\omega t+\pi), \\[6pt]
v_c'(t) &= \sqrt{2}r\big[\cos(\omega t+\phi+120^\circ+\pi)+\cos(\omega t-\phi+240^\circ)\big]\\
&= 2\sqrt{2}r\sin(\phi-60^\circ)\sin(\omega t+\pi).
\end{aligned} $$

**Key takeaways:**

- Flipping $V_1$ rotates the entire set by 90° in time (cos → sin), and changes the amplitude weights from $\cos(\cdot)$ to $\sin(\cdot)$.
    
- It does not make the sources vanish (except at special $\phi$ values, a single phase at a single instant can be zero — that's normal).
    


## Quick table (equal magnitudes)

| Case       | $v_a(t)$                         | $v_b(t)$                                              | $v_c(t)$                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| No flip    | $2\sqrt{2}r\cos\phi\cos\omega t$ | $2\sqrt{2}r\cos(\phi{+}60^\circ)\cos(\omega t{+}\pi)$ | $2\sqrt{2}r\cos(\phi{-}60^\circ)\cos(\omega t{+}\pi)$ |
| Flip $V_1$ | $2\sqrt{2}r\sin\phi\sin\omega t$ | $2\sqrt{2}r\sin(\phi{+}60^\circ)\sin(\omega t{+}\pi)$ | $2\sqrt{2}r\sin(\phi{-}60^\circ)\sin(\omega t{+}\pi)$ |
